info.text:
In Sept 2026, 10 companies made up about 40% of the S&P 500.

The S&P 500 (kept since 1957) is a basket of 500 big US companies, weighted by market value, so big companies count more. In a hypothetical $60T basket, a $3T company is 5%; a $30B company is 0.05%.
To join, a company generally must be US-based, profitable and big enough; a committee decides.
Year-end close: 3,839.50 in 2022; 6,845.50 in 2025.

Sources: S&P Dow Jones Indices; RBC Wealth Management; index weight trackers (Sept 2026).
News and education, not financial advice.
